<reason>Both sides were forensic and quotable, but B kept the single decisive comparison alive to the end: under licensing, unresolved uncertainty about an irrecoverable capability defaults to no market access; under CON's regime it defaults to release on the developer's own conformity assessment. A's best weapons — the "name the finding" fork, the liability-shield/state-stamp turn, the GDPR architecture turn (genuinely unanswered by B), and the moat objection — were sharp, and A pressed hard on the motion's "move from" wording. But B answered the two hardest pressures directly and with labels: it named a workable statutory test (applicant must demonstrate competently run dangerous-capability evaluations against published thresholds; refusal ground is failure to demonstrate, on an EMA-style burden), and it defused the "you kept the use-level duties" gotcha as background law surviving in every licensed sector, which is a textually defensible reading of the motion's own scope clause. A's honest but costly concession that "under neither regime does a gate stop it" narrowed its case to a cost/futility claim, and B's chokepoint reply (harm scales through lawful institutional deployment into hospitals, banks, ministries and cloud; no garage frontier labs at hundreds of millions per training run) was reasserted-against rather than dismantled: A's closing re-stated "refuse whose entry?" without engaging the claim that the most capable models are precisely the ones seeking lawful European deployment. A had the last word and used it well, which keeps this close, but the marginal-benefit question (self-certified release vs. authority-approved release) was resolved in B's favour.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's Rebuttal 2 answer [B4.3]-[B4.4], which met A's "name the statutory test" challenge with a demonstrate-adequate-testing standard and then flipped it into the default-under-uncertainty comparison ("uncertainty defaults to no access; under CON it defaults to the market"), simultaneously answering the fork and reframing the weighing.</best_rebuttal>
